meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT Exemplar solution proving tan(½ sin⁻¹ 3/4) = (4−√7)/3, with the reason the other root is rejected, plus a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Half-Angle Inverse Trig Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on tan of half a sin⁻¹, the range and quadrant of sin⁻¹, and rejecting the extraneous root. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: tan(½ sin⁻¹ x) and half-angle inverse trigonometry (Class 12)

questions.q: What is the principal value range of sin⁻¹ x?
questions.explanation: By definition sin⁻¹ returns an angle in [−π/2, π/2]. That range is what fixes the sign of every later step in this problem.

questions.q: If θ = sin⁻¹(3/4), what is cos θ?
questions.explanation: sin θ = 3/4, so cos θ = √(1 − 9/16) = √7/4. It is positive because θ lies in the first quadrant, where cosine is positive.

questions.q: For θ = sin⁻¹(3/4), in which interval does θ/2 lie?
questions.explanation: Since 3/4 > 0, θ is in (0, π/2), so θ/2 is in (0, π/4). This is the fact that later lets you throw out one root.

questions.q: Writing t = tan(θ/2) and sin θ = 2t/(1+t²), which equation does sin θ = 3/4 give?

options: Because tangent is negative in this quadrant
Because θ/2 ∈ (0, π/4), so tan(θ/2) < 1, but (4 + √7)/3 > 1
Because it is an irrational number
questions.explanation: θ/2 lies in (0, π/4), where tan is between 0 and 1. Since (4 + √7)/3 ≈ 2.22 > 1, it cannot be tan(θ/2), so only (4 − √7)/3 survives.

questions.q: What is the value of tan(½ sin⁻¹(3/4))?
questions.explanation: The accepted root is (4 − √7)/3 ≈ 0.45, which correctly sits between 0 and 1 as required for an angle in (0, π/4).

questions.q: In terms of t = tan(θ/2), how is tan θ expressed?
questions.explanation: The double-angle identity gives tan θ = 2t/(1 − t²). Note 2t/(1 + t²) is sin θ, not tan θ — a common mix-up.

faq.q: Why does sin⁻¹(3/4) land in the first quadrant?
faq.a: The principal value of sin⁻¹ is always in [−π/2, π/2]. Since 3/4 is positive, the angle is in (0, π/2), the first quadrant, so both its cosine and its half-angle tangent are positive.

faq.q: Where does the quadratic 3t² − 8t + 3 = 0 come from?
faq.a: Set t = tan(θ/2). Using sin θ = 2t/(1+t²) and sin θ = 3/4 gives 8t = 3(1+t²), which rearranges into 3t² − 8t + 3 = 0. Solving it produces the two candidate values.

faq.q: How do you decide which root to keep?
faq.a: θ/2 lies in (0, π/4), so tan(θ/2) must be between 0 and 1. Of the two roots, (4 + √7)/3 ≈ 2.22 is greater than 1 and impossible, while (4 − √7)/3 ≈ 0.45 fits, so it is the answer.

faq.q: Can this be solved without the half-angle formula?
faq.a: Yes. You can use tan(θ/2) = sin θ / (1 + cos θ). With sin θ = 3/4 and cos θ = √7/4 you get (3/4)/(1 + √7/4) = 3/(4 + √7), which rationalises to (4 − √7)/3 — the same answer, no rejection needed.
